title: communication_log
description: One line in the send log: one attempt to tell one person one thing, with what came of it (see CMS_GUIDE.md and COMMUNICATION_LOG_GUIDE.md). Written only by the server (the CMS), once per recipient per call, whatever the outcome. The message text is never stored: the kind, the template version and the facts identify what was sent. Append-only, with one exception: an operator marks a not_sent entry handled (the handled_ fields), and later provider status may be attached. The per-attendance and per-request message history is a view of these entries. Rules the schema cannot express: entries are written only by the server; create, update and soft delete through the endpoints are refused (only get, list and the mark-handled operation work); merging two people repoints individual_id; erasing a person removes what describes the entry (to, subject, handled_note) and leaves an anonymous tombstone.
x_retention: Kept. When the individual is erased the entry is soft deleted and everything that describes it is removed, leaving an anonymous tombstone. (A written policy only; the erase code does it. Same policy as attendance, P-08.)

kind.description: The message kind attempted, such as placement_confirmation. Required.

template_version.description: The version number of the template used. Absent when no template was found or the attempt stopped before that step.

audience.description: The audience label the caller gave. Optional.

individual_id.description: The person told, when the recipient was a known individual. Optional. Not checked. Repointed when people are merged.

channel.description: The channel used or chosen: email, text, or none when no channel could be chosen. Required.

to.description: The address or number the message went to (the redirect address when a test redirect was on). Absent when there was none. Personal data.

is_redirected.description: true when the test redirect replaced the real address. Absent means false.

subject.description: The subject line as sent, or the title for a non-email channel. Absent when nothing was rendered. Personal data.

status.description: What came of it: sent (the provider accepted it), failed (the provider refused it), unknown (no answer in time), not_sent (the CMS wanted to send and could not, so a person may need to act) or skipped (the CMS decided not to send). Required.

reason.description: The closed reason code. Each reason belongs to exactly one status: ok is sent; adapter_error is failed; timeout is unknown; unknown_kind, invalid_context, no_contact, channel_unavailable, no_template, incomplete, time_budget and internal_error (a bug in the CMS itself, caught so the caller is never hurt) are not_sent; cms_off, log_only, duplicate, excluded and muted are skipped. Required.

error_code.description: A short sanitized code from the provider or adapter, for failed and unknown entries. Never a reply text. Optional.

message_ref.description: The Message-ID the CMS put on the email, so the provider's delivered, bounced and opened reports can be matched later. Optional.

trigger.description: automatic (the product decided) or manual (an operator pressed a button). Required.

request_id.description: The registration request this message belongs to. Optional. Not checked.

scheduled_class_id.description: The class this message belongs to. Optional. Not checked.

attendance_id.description: The attendance record this message belongs to. Optional. Not checked.

dedupe_key.description: The key that stops the same event being sent twice. Optional.

contract_version.description: The version of the CMS call contract the call used. Required.

handled_at.description: When an operator marked this not_sent entry as dealt with (UTC). Absent until then. Set by the server.

handled_by.description: Who marked it handled, as an actor string. Set by the server.

handled_note.description: What the operator did, such as called by hand. Up to 500 characters. Personal data. Optional.

id.description: UUID v4, set by the server; also the Firestore document id.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema the record was written under (currently 1). Set by the server.

created_at.description: When the record was created (UTC). Set by the server. For a log entry this is when the attempt happened.

created_by.description: Who created it, as an actor string. Set by the server.

updated_at.description: When the record last changed (UTC). Set by the server.

updated_by.description: Who last changed it. Set by the server.

source.description: Where the record came from: dashboard or import. Set by the server.

deleted_at.description: When the record was soft deleted (UTC); absent while live. Set by the server.

deleted_by.description: Who soft deleted it. Set by the server.
